title: Mutation Governance Boundary — which authority governs which class of mutation
authority: AUTHORED REPOSITORY TRUTH, HELD SUBORDINATE UNDER UCKP-LAW-0001. This artifact declares the boundary; it does not create a new authority and governs nothing itself.

constitutional_superior.effect: This artifact already said of itself that it creates no authority and governs nothing. UCKP-ART-10 — execution never owns knowledge — is the article that sentence is true UNDER. It owns which mutation classes exist and which authority disposes of each; it may never own knowledge.

constitutional_basis: UCKP-LAW-0001 (engine/uckp/law.py), UCOS-CAA-001, UCOS-CMG-EXEC-000001 Requirement 004, GOV-005, UCOS-CL-016
determination: OPTION B — SOURCE MUTATIONS ARE OUTSIDE THE CONSTITUTIONAL MUTATION GATEWAY
why_this_determination: The question was live because a source mutation (be46a300, touching intelligence/rie/evidence.py,
scripts/ucos-env.sh and .gitignore) was applied with no gateway record, and the closure matrix
could not say whether that was a bypass or simply out of scope.
It is out of scope, and the evidence is structural rather than interpretive:
`ConstitutionalMetadata` values. Its stages take a `Context` holding `base` and
`candidate` populations, and `apply()` returns a new population plus a StateSeal.
* Neither gateway.py nor state.py imports `pathlib`, opens a file, reads or writes text,
or invokes git. Measured directly: a search for Path / open( / read_text / write_text /
git across both modules returns nothing.
* Its enforcement mechanism is that it is the ONLY producer of a clean StateSeal, and
engine.constitution.state refuses to verify, certify, register, measure or govern under a
dirty or mismatched seal. That mechanism binds constitutional TRUTH operations. There is
no seal check anywhere on the path that writes a .py file to disk, and adding one would
require the gateway to grow a filesystem it deliberately does not have.
So CMG governs mutations of CONSTITUTIONAL TRUTH — law, population, metadata, registry state.
A source-file mutation is a different class of act, and the repository already governs it, but
through a chain that had never been written down. That absence is what made the earlier bypass
unanswerable. It is written down here.

authorities.enforcement: sole producer of a clean StateSeal; engine.constitution.state refuses the five truth operations without one

governs: the INTENDED MUTATION boundary — tracked/staged source content at commit time
lint and format of the governed source roots
governance enforcement, registry schema validation, meta-constitutional conformance
authorities.enforcement: non-zero exit on any failing stage

governs: repository integrity including the git object database (GATE-02)
filesystem contamination and exclusion classification (GATE-12, VAL-11, VAL-12)
convergence of the observation vector across iterations (CONV-01..07)
does_not_govern: byte-level repository closure — explicitly disclaimed in its own certification (AEE-F-002)

governs: byte-level idempotence of the canonical chain across consecutive rounds
reproduction of canonical artifacts from a clean clone of the certified commit
does_not_govern: environmental observational outputs explicitly classified non-canonical

mutation_classes.governed_by: pre-commit → verify.sh → UCOS-RIB-001 → UCOS-AEE-001 → Phase 8 → Phase 9

invariants: Every mutation class names exactly one governing authority chain.
No mutation class is claimed by two authorities as primary.
No mutation class is ungoverned — there is no class whose governed_by is empty.
Every named authority resolves to an implementation that exists in the tree.
The EXCLUSION class is governed by a register, never by the exclusion mechanism itself — this is the UCOS-CL-001 correction stated as a boundary rule.
recurrence_prevention: The bypass at be46a300 was not a rule violation; it was an undeclared boundary. A source
mutation had no gateway to take and no written statement that it did not need one, so the
question could only be answered by reading the gateway's imports. This artifact makes the
answer declarative and testable: test_mutation_governance_boundary.py asserts that every
class is governed, that no class is doubly claimed, and that every named implementation
exists. A future mutation class added without an authority fails that test.
